title: Build a generic Stack in Rust
description: Greenfield Rust task: implement a generic Stack<T> with push, pop, peek, is_empty, and len operations.

task_spec.prompt:
Implement Stack<T> in src/lib.rs.

pub struct Stack<T> {
    data: Vec<T>,
}

impl<T> Stack<T> {
    pub fn new() -> Self
    pub fn push(&mut self, item: T)
    pub fn pop(&mut self) -> Option<T>    // removes and returns top element
    pub fn peek(&self) -> Option<&T>      // borrows top element without removing
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize
}

Backed by a Vec<T>; push appends to the end, pop removes from the end (LIFO).
All 5 tests in tests/stack_test.rs must pass.
Run: cargo test
required_artifacts: pop returns None on empty stack
peek returns borrowed reference to top element
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `cargo test` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
